subject: math

entries: Meet the 3-4-5 triangle: name the sides from angle theta first - opposite = 3, adjacent = 4, hypotenuse = 5 - then sine is opposite over hypotenuse, sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6.
slots.label: Meet the 3-4-5 triangle
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: Cosine and tangent join the card: cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8 (adjacent over hypotenuse) and tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75 (opposite over adjacent) - read the whole card as SOH CAH TOA.
slots.label: Cosine and tangent join the card
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The sine rule for any triangle: a / sin A = b / sin B pairs each side with its opposite angle, so with a = 4, A = 30 degrees and B = 60 degrees, b comes out to about 6.93.
slots.label: The sine rule for any triangle
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: A common mistake: do not flip tangent: the flipped ratio 4/3 = 1.33 is taller than the whole, while the correct TOA ratio 3/4 = 0.75 sits properly inside it.
slots.label: A common mistake
slots.studentPrompt: Explain this step in your own words.

entries: The ratio opposite over hypotenuse for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, sin theta = 3/5 = 0.6 (the SOH part of the card).
slots.label: Sine
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The ratio adjacent over hypotenuse for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, cos theta = 4/5 = 0.8 (the CAH part of the card).
slots.label: Cosine
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The ratio opposite over adjacent for an angle in a right-angled triangle: in the 3-4-5 triangle, tan theta = 3/4 = 0.75 (the TOA part of the card).
slots.label: Tangent
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The longest side of a right-angled triangle, across from the right angle: length 5 in the 3-4-5 triangle.
slots.label: Hypotenuse
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The side across from the angle you are working with: length 3 for angle theta in the 3-4-5 triangle.
slots.label: Opposite
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The side next to the angle you are working with, other than the hypotenuse: length 4 for angle theta in the 3-4-5 triangle.
slots.label: Adjacent
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

entries: The rule a / sin A = b / sin B, linking each side of any triangle with the sine of its opposite angle, used when there is no right angle.
slots.label: Sine rule
slots.studentPrompt: Give your own example of this term.

title: E-Math trigonometry: ratios and the sine rule
